name: Ollama
description: One command to download and serve open LLMs on your own machine with an OpenAI-compatible API.
long_description: Ollama makes local models practical: it handles downloads, quantisation and GPU offloading, and exposes an HTTP API that most AI tooling can point at. Everything runs offline at no cost beyond your own hardware.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed and free; unlimited local inference on your own hardware.
best_for: Private inference with no per-token cost
Powering free coding assistants like Cline or Continue
not_ideal_for: Frontier-model quality on a laptop
Very large models without significant RAM or VRAM

free_access.description: Unlimited local inference with no account or key.
restrictions: Model quality is limited by your hardware

name: LM Studio
description: Graphical way to discover, run and serve local models, including for commercial work.
long_description: LM Studio provides a chat interface, model browser and a local OpenAI-compatible server without touching the command line. It is free to use, including at work, which makes it an easy entry point for local AI.
free_access_summary: Free to use, including for commercial work; runs entirely on your machine.
best_for: Trying local models without the terminal
not_ideal_for: Server deployments - it is a desktop application

free_access.description: Free for personal and commercial use.

name: Hugging Face
description: Hosts open models, datasets and demos, with free accounts and a free inference allowance.
long_description: Hugging Face is the default distribution point for open models and datasets, with Spaces for demos and an inference API. Free accounts get unlimited public repositories and a monthly inference credit allowance.
free_access_summary: Free account with unlimited public repositories and a monthly inference credit allowance.
pricing_summary: Paid Pro accounts and usage-based compute are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
not_ideal_for: High-throughput production inference on the free allowance

free_access.description: Monthly inference credit allowance on free accounts, plus unlimited public repositories.
restrictions: Spaces run on shared CPU hardware

name: Google AI Studio
description: Browser playground for Gemini models with a free API tier for developers.
long_description: AI Studio lets you prototype prompts, tune parameters and export code, then call the same models through the Gemini API. The free tier is generous enough to build and test real features before paying anything.
free_access_summary: Free API tier with per-minute and per-day request limits; no credit card required to start.
best_for: Building AI features with no upfront cost
not_ideal_for: Production traffic beyond the free rate limits

free_access.description: Free tier with per-minute and daily request limits that vary by model.
restrictions: Free tier data may be used to improve products in some regions

name: Groq
description: Runs open models at exceptionally high token throughput, with a free developer tier.
long_description: Groq's custom hardware delivers responses fast enough to change what feels possible in interactive applications. A free tier with rate limits lets developers build against it without payment details.
free_access_summary: Free developer tier with rate-limited access to open models.
not_ideal_for: Access to proprietary frontier models

free_access.description: Free tier with per-minute and per-day request and token limits.

name: OpenRouter
description: Single OpenAI-compatible endpoint routing to hundreds of models, including free ones.
long_description: OpenRouter lets you switch models without changing code and exposes a set of genuinely free models alongside paid ones, with transparent per-token pricing and automatic failover.
free_access_summary: A set of free models is available with rate limits; paid models are pay-as-you-go.
best_for: Powering free coding agents such as Cline
not_ideal_for: Guaranteed capacity on free models

free_access.description: Free model variants with daily request limits.
restrictions: Free models have lower rate limits
Availability of free models changes over time

name: Together AI
description: Hosted inference for open models with free starting credits and fine-tuning support.
long_description: Together AI serves a wide catalogue of open models with an OpenAI-compatible API and provides fine-tuning and dedicated endpoints. New accounts receive starting credits.
free_access_summary: Free starting credits for new accounts; usage is metered afterwards.
best_for: Running open models at scale without owning GPUs
not_ideal_for: Long-term free usage - credits are one-off

free_access.description: One-time credit grant for new accounts.

name: OpenAI Platform
description: Pay-as-you-go API for OpenAI models, embeddings, images, audio and agents.
long_description: The OpenAI API provides text, embedding, image and audio models plus agent tooling. There is no ongoing free tier: usage is billed per token, so treat it as a paid dependency.
free_access_summary: No ongoing free tier. Usage is billed per token.
pricing_summary: Per-token pricing varies by model. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Broadest feature coverage in one API
not_ideal_for: Projects that must stay at zero cost

name: LangChain
description: Open source toolkit for chaining models, tools and retrieval into applications.
long_description: LangChain provides the plumbing for LLM applications - prompt templates, tool calling, memory, retrievers and agent loops - across Python and JavaScript, with adapters for most providers and vector stores.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed framework; the optional hosted observability platform has a free tier.
not_ideal_for: Simple single-prompt scripts where the abstraction is overhead

free_access.description: The framework is open source and free.

name: LlamaIndex
description: Open source framework for indexing your data and querying it with an LLM.
long_description: LlamaIndex specialises in the retrieval half of RAG: loading documents, chunking, indexing into vector stores and composing query engines. It has a large connector library for real-world data sources.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed and free; hosted parsing services have a free allowance.
not_ideal_for: Use cases with no retrieval component

free_access.description: Open source and free to use.
restrictions: Managed parsing service has usage limits
Model and vector store costs are separate

name: Chroma
description: Open source vector store that runs in-process, ideal for local RAG development.
long_description: Chroma is designed to be the simplest possible vector database: pip install, add documents, query. It runs embedded or as a server, which makes it a natural first step before committing to hosted infrastructure.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free to run locally or self-hosted.
not_ideal_for: Billion-scale vector workloads

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: Hosted cloud offering is billed separately

name: Qdrant
description: Rust-based vector search engine with rich filtering, open source and a free cloud tier.
long_description: Qdrant combines vector similarity with strict payload filtering, which matters when retrieval must respect tenancy or permissions. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and offers a free managed cluster.
free_access_summary: Open source, plus a permanently free 1GB managed cluster.
not_ideal_for: Projects wanting an in-process embedded store

free_access.description: Free managed cluster with 1GB of storage, plus unlimited self-hosting.
restrictions: No SLA on the free tier

name: Weaviate
description: Vector database with built-in vectorisation modules and hybrid search.
long_description: Weaviate can generate embeddings itself through modules, supports hybrid keyword and vector search, and offers GraphQL and REST APIs. It is open source with a free sandbox cloud instance.
free_access_summary: BSD licensed and self-hostable; a free sandbox cluster is available.
not_ideal_for: Very small projects that need no server

free_access.description: Open source and free to self-host; free sandbox clusters expire.

name: Pinecone
description: Fully managed vector search with a free starter index and no infrastructure to run.
long_description: Pinecone removes operational work from vector search: no cluster sizing, no upgrades. The free Starter tier supports a real index, which is enough for a prototype or small production feature.
free_access_summary: Free Starter plan with a limited serverless index and monthly operation limits.
pricing_summary: Usage-based paid plans are available. Check the official pricing page for current rates.
best_for: Teams that do not want to operate a database
not_ideal_for: Air-gapped or self-hosted requirements

free_access.description: Free Starter plan with a capped serverless index and monthly read and write units.

name: Model Context Protocol
tagline: Open standard for AI tool access
description: The open protocol and SDKs that let assistants call your tools, data and services.
long_description: MCP standardises how an AI client connects to external tools and data sources, so one server works across Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other clients. The specification and SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Java and more are open source.
free_access_summary: Open specification and SDKs, free to implement and self-host.
best_for: Exposing internal systems to AI assistants
Writing one integration for many clients
not_ideal_for: Teams wanting a finished product rather than a protocol

free_access.description: Open specification and SDKs under permissive licences.
restrictions: You build and host your own servers

name: n8n
description: Source-available automation platform with LLM nodes, self-hostable for free.
long_description: n8n connects hundreds of services in a visual workflow and includes AI agent nodes with tool calling and memory. Self-hosting under the fair-code licence is free and keeps data on your infrastructure.
free_access_summary: Source available and free to self-host; the managed cloud is paid after a trial.
capabilities: Code nodes in JavaScript and Python
best_for: Automating internal processes with AI steps
not_ideal_for: Teams without anywhere to host it who want a free cloud tier

free_access.description: Free to self-host under the sustainable use licence.

name: Dify
description: Visual builder for RAG pipelines, agents and workflows that you can self-host.
long_description: Dify combines a prompt IDE, RAG pipeline, agent framework and observability in one self-hostable platform, exposing finished apps as APIs. It suits teams that want to iterate on AI features without building infrastructure first.
free_access_summary: Open source and free to self-host; the hosted sandbox plan is free with limits.
not_ideal_for: Highly custom pipelines better written in code

free_access.description: Free to self-host; hosted sandbox includes limited trial messages.

name: Flowise
description: Open source visual builder for chains, agents and RAG pipelines on top of LangChain.
long_description: Flowise gives a node-based interface over LangChain and LlamaIndex primitives, then exposes the result as an API or embeddable chat widget. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and runs anywhere Node runs.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free to self-host.
not_ideal_for: Complex logic that belongs in version-controlled code

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: Cloud hosting is a paid convenience

name: CrewAI
description: Python framework for teams of role-playing agents that collaborate on a task.
long_description: CrewAI models agents as roles with goals and tools, coordinating them through sequential or hierarchical processes. It is open source and independent of any single model provider.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed framework, free to use with any model.
not_ideal_for: Single-step tasks where one prompt suffices

free_access.description: Free and open source.
restrictions: Model usage billed by your provider

name: vLLM
description: Open source inference server that dramatically increases throughput for self-hosted models.
long_description: vLLM introduced paged attention and continuous batching, which make self-hosted serving far more efficient. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so existing clients work unchanged.
free_access_summary: Apache-2.0 licensed and free; you provide the GPUs.
best_for: Getting more throughput from existing GPUs
not_ideal_for: Laptops and CPU-only environments

free_access.description: Free and open source.

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
description: Run open models from serverless functions with a free daily allowance.
long_description: Workers AI runs open models on Cloudflare's edge network, callable from Workers or over HTTP. The free tier includes a daily neuron allowance, which is enough for prototypes and light production use.
free_access_summary: Free daily inference allowance included with a Cloudflare account.
not_ideal_for: Frontier proprietary models

free_access.description: Daily free neuron allowance across models.
restrictions: Model catalogue is limited to supported open models

name: AnythingLLM
description: Desktop and self-hosted app that turns your documents into a private chat workspace.
long_description: AnythingLLM bundles document ingestion, a vector store and a chat interface into a single application that can run fully offline with Ollama. Everything stays on your machine, which makes it suitable for confidential material.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed; the desktop application is free and works fully offline.
best_for: Private question answering over internal documents
not_ideal_for: Embedding retrieval into your own product - use a framework instead

free_access.description: Free desktop app and self-hosted deployment.
restrictions: Cloud hosting is a paid option
